t:
(a) 
In General.—
Section 44721 of title 49, United States Code, is amended—

        (1) 
by striking paragraphs (3) and (4) of subsection (c); and
 
        (2) 
by adding at the end of subsection (g)(1) the following:


“(D) 
Continuation of prices.—
The price of any product created under subsection (d) may correspond to the price of a comparable product produced by a department of the United States Government as that price was in effect on September 30, 2000, and may remain in effect until modified by regulation under section 9701 of title 31, United States Code.”
; and

 
        (3) 
by adding at the end of subsection (g) the following:


“(5) 
Crediting amounts received.—
Notwithstanding any other provision of law, amounts received for the sale of products created and services performed under this section shall be fully credited to the account of the Federal Aviation Administration that funded the provision of the products or services and shall remain available until expended.”
.

  
    (b) 
Effective Date.—
The amendments made by subsection (a) take effect on October 1, 2000.

fable.w: The tempting reading is that this is a purely internal pricing and accounting amendment with no outside party involved, and the crediting and effective-date provisions are indeed not participatory. However, the continuation-of-prices clause says the price stays in effect until it is modified by regulation, which channels any future price change through agency rulemaking. Under the definition, authorizing or requiring rulemaking counts as participation. This is a close call because the clause refers to existing regulatory authority under 31 U.S.C. 9701 rather than creating a new rulemaking mandate.
fable.s: may remain in effect until modified by regulation under section 9701 of title 31, United States Code.

opus.w: The section makes rulemaking the way to change FAA product prices: they stay in effect 'until modified by regulation.' Under the definition and Example 6, a statute that requires or authorizes regulations counts as participation, because rulemaking brings in outside comment. The tempting 'No' reading treats the section as pure fiscal housekeeping, but the regulation requirement is a real rulemaking hook. It is borderline because the section points to regulations under another law rather than granting new authority itself.
opus.s: may remain in effect until modified by regulation under section 9701 of title 31, United States Code.
opus.b:
I labelled this **Yes**, but it's a borderline call.

1. **Why "No" is tempting:** Most of the section is about money: striking paragraphs, keeping old product prices, and crediting sales receipts to an FAA account. None of it names outside parties, hearings or consultation.
2. **Why "Yes" anyway:** The new subparagraph (D) says the prices stay in effect "until modified by regulation under section 9701 of title 31." That means any future price change must go through rulemaking. The definition counts requiring rulemaking as participation, because rulemaking normally brings in public comment. Example 6 counted even optional "may by regulation" authority as participation.
3. **Why confidence is moderate:** The section only refers to regulations under another law rather than granting new rulemaking authority itself, so a stricter reading could come out "No."

qwen_chat.w: This section deals with internal federal accounting and pricing rules for products and services provided by the Federal Aviation Administration. It does not require or recommend consultation, coordination, or input from any non-federal entities (such as the public, states, tribes, or private companies) in making decisions. All actors mentioned (FAA, US Government departments) are inside the federal government.
qwen_chat.s: Notwithstanding any other provision of law, amounts received for the sale of products created and services performed under this section shall be fully credited to the account of the Federal Aviation Administration that funded the provision of the products or services and shall remain available until expended.
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that "participation" is involved because the text mentions "products created under subsection (d)" or "services performed," implying some external interaction. However, the text itself only describes internal accounting rules (crediting amounts to an FAA account) and pricing mechanisms for government-produced products. There is no mention of consulting with, coordinating with, or allowing input from any non-federal entity (such as the public, states, tribes, or private companies) in the decision-making process described in this specific section. The actors are entirely within the federal government (FAA, Department of the US Government).
